answer: Give each identity only after a verifiable delay function, a sequential puzzle no hardware can speed up. First, the agent gets a unique seed. Second, it computes for 24 straight hours, a slow climb across an umber tundra to a distant summit, impossible to split. Third, the network checks the proof in seconds and stamps the identity. Fourth, a caught sybil starts over from zero. Faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 machines for a full day each, about 50,000 dollars of power and hardware time. Like a mountain pass, the road is open to anyone willing to walk it, closed to shortcut hunters.
